 Key Takeaways
 When a refund advance isn’t an option, I’d start with these services to explore alternatives.
 24/7 Lending Group : Best for exploring personal loan offers across a range of credit backgrounds.
 MoneyMutual : Best for exploring smaller, short-term loans while waiting for your refund.
 When life happens, it rarely considers your bank account. Mine certainly doesn’t get a warning. If you need cash fast, you may not have the luxury of waiting for your tax refund. A tax refund advance might help, but only if you qualify and apply while the offer’s still open.
 Otherwise, you still have options. To help narrow your search, I looked into five tax refund advance alternatives, including personal loans and a paycheck advance that may help cover expenses while you wait.
 Personal Loan Alternatives to a Tax Refund Advance
 Before choosing a tax refund advance, I’d check the total cost, including any interest and tax preparation fees. You may be required to use the participating tax preparation service to file your taxes, taking even more out of your refund. As you can imagine, it can get expensive fast.

 You can usually get your loan directly from a lender or through a lending platform that works with a network of lenders (like Upstart ). 
 However, one thing I’d watch closely is how each lender’s terms and requirements differ. That can complicate your search when you don’t have time to waste.
 To give you a shortcut, I’ve outlined the best tax refund advance alternatives based on credit requirements, loan amounts and terms. With these top picks, you can explore borrowing options while you wait for your refund, and repayment follows the provider’s terms even if your refund is delayed or smaller than expected.
 With every lender offering its own terms and loan amounts, I’d take the time to run the numbers and calculate the repayment costs. For example, lenders available through 24/7 Lending Group may offer terms up to 72 months, but with Avant , there are only terms of up to 60 months. A longer term may lower your monthly payment but increase your total interest cost.
 A loan calculator, like this one from the Office of Financial Readiness, is where I’d start to estimate payments so you can check to make sure you can repay your loan, even if your refund is late or smaller than expected.
 A Paycheck Advance Alternative While You Wait for Your Refund 
 As we’ve discussed, a tax refund advance won’t work for everyone, but you have another option in the form of a paycheck advance loan . This is a short-term loan that gives you cash that you pay back using your paycheck instead of your tax refund.  
 Current is another option while you wait for your refund, with eligibility based on factors other than your credit score . For me, that makes it worth a look if credit is your main concern.

 To qualify for Paycheck Advance from Current , you generally need eligible payroll deposits into your Current account. The advance is typically repaid automatically from your next payroll deposit. Funding speed and any expedited funding fee depend on the option you select.
 My advice is to run the numbers and always, always review the fine print. Armed with this knowledge, you can better determine whether a paycheck advance will work until your next paycheck. Just be careful that you don’t set yourself up for failure by taking out a loan you can’t repay. 
 What Is a Tax Refund Advance and How Does It Work? 
 A tax refund advance helps pay the bills when your tax refund hasn’t come yet. But does a tax refund advance really help, and how do you get one? 
 A tax refund advance is a short-term loan based on your estimated refund. Before applying, I’d check how much the provider may offer and what it costs.
 Unfortunately, this advance won’t make the IRS process your return any faster , but at least you can borrow against those funds in the meantime. Then, when your check comes in, you simply repay your loan. This may be with or without interest , depending on your lender. 
 Where Does My Refund Go?
 Example only. Actual amounts and fees vary. The advance is part of your refund received early, not extra money.

 Actual tax refund

 $(150.00)

 $1,350.00 
 Your tax preparer may offer you a refund anticipation check (RAC) as another option. With this, you won’t pay tax preparation fees until you get your refund. However, a RAC isn’t a loan and doesn’t provide money before your refund arrives. It usually carries an additional fee.
 Before choosing between a tax refund advance and an alternative, I’d break out the magnifying glass and examine the fine print, including fees, interest and penalties. This will help you determine if you can even afford to take out a loan. 
 After all, the last thing you want is to fall behind on your loan, thus increasing your debt instead of reducing it.  
 Can I Get a Tax Refund Advance After Filing My Taxes?
 If you’ve already filed your return, you generally can’t add a refund advance through a different tax preparation company. Most programs require you to select the advance through that provider’s filing process.
 Some programs release funds after the IRS accepts your return, while certain early advance programs are available before filing season. Requirements vary by provider. Before making a trip, I’d check the provider’s application window.
 With all these requirements, you need to get a jump-start on your taxes before tax season. If you don’t apply during the specific window, a personal loan could be the answer to the funds you need. If you can qualify, it can be a great strategy to avoid financial hardship until you receive your tax refund. 
 Already filed? I’d check the IRS refund status tool before deciding whether to borrow.
 Can I Get a Tax Refund Advance Online With No Credit Check? 
 Some tax refund advance programs don’t require a hard credit inquiry , but approval and credit requirements vary by provider. These loans aren’t guaranteed by the U.S. government. 
 Your expected refund helps determine eligibility and the amount you may qualify to borrow. Bad credit doesn’t automatically disqualify you, but approval isn’t guaranteed.
 Before sharing my information, I’d check whether the provider uses a soft or hard credit inquiry. A hard inquiry may affect your credit score.
 For alternatives that consider a range of credit backgrounds, my starting points are 24/7 Lending Group and MoneyMutual . Both connect borrowers with potential lenders rather than providing refund advances themselves.
 Paying a tax preparer doesn’t guarantee approval for an advance.
 Can I Get a Tax Refund Advance Online Today? 
 You may be able to get a tax refund advance online when a provider’s application window is open. You’ll need to meet its eligibility requirements and apply through its tax filing process.
 Before You Apply
 Credit inquiry: Will the provider use a soft or hard inquiry?
 Approval: Paying for tax preparation doesn’t guarantee an advance.
 Repayment: What happens if your refund is delayed or smaller than expected?
 After approval, you could get your funds soon after the IRS accepts your return, depending on the program. Many lenders require a specific bank account or a prepaid debit card . For me, that’s another detail to check before applying.
 As you start to think about filing your tax return, don’t forget to consider these tax refund advance alternatives, as well. 
 How Do H&R Block and TurboTax Refund Advances Compare With Alternatives? 
 The appeal of H&R Block and TurboTax, to me, is being able to file your taxes and apply for a refund advance through the same company. But application windows, eligibility requirements and advance amounts can change each tax season, so I’d check the current terms before choosing a filing service.
 Some refund advances have no loan fees or interest, although tax preparation and optional services may cost extra. A personal loan or paycheck advance has a different cost structure, so compare the total cost of getting the money you need.
 What to compare Tax refund advance Personal loan alternative Paycheck advance 
 When to apply During the provider’s seasonal window Generally available throughout the year When eligible through the provider 
 Filing requirement Usually tied to a participating tax preparation service Doesn’t require using a particular tax preparer Based on payroll eligibility 
 Repayment Generally deducted from your refund Scheduled payments under the loan agreement Generally collected from an upcoming paycheck 
 Costs to check Loan charges, preparation costs and optional services APR and any loan fees Any subscription or expedited funding fees 
 Before paying for tax preparation, I’d confirm whether the advance is available and whether you meet the requirements. Paying a preparer doesn’t guarantee loan approval.
 If you’ve already filed elsewhere or missed the application window, the alternatives above may still be worth exploring. My main concern would be whether repayment fits your budget, even if your refund is delayed or smaller than expected.
 Choose a Tax Refund Advance Alternative That Fits Your Budget 
 Before applying for an advance, I recommend checking the provider’s application window, filing requirements and costs. Your estimated refund and the provider’s underwriting will help determine how much you may qualify to borrow.
 For me, the next step is adding up the costs so you can confirm that the tax refund alternative you choose actually matches your budget . In addition to interest , you may encounter fees like tax preparation fees, funding fees and finance charges. 
 This could become problematic if your refund is less than the total cost of your advance. If your refund is less than you were expecting, what happens to any unpaid balance depends on your loan agreement . With a separate personal loan, you still owe the scheduled payments regardless of your refund.
 My Before-You-Borrow Checklist
 ☐ Check the deadline: When is the first payment or automatic deduction?
 ☐ Add up the cost: What will you pay in interest, loan fees and optional charges?
 ☐ Plan for a smaller refund: Could you still make the required payments?
 ☐ Protect your next paycheck: Will enough remain for rent, groceries and other bills?
 ☐ Consider a payment extension: Could more time to pay the original bill avoid borrowing?
 If you can’t wait, a tax refund advance or alternative can be a quick way to get cash if you can qualify and afford the repayment terms. Just remember: a refund advance reduces the refund you receive later, while a separate loan comes with its own repayment schedule.
